To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a process model is a description of a solution for a problem, which is composed from a set of generic patterns; 2) a process-centred system is a computer system that provides a set of services for the management of a process model, which is composed of a set of generic services; and 3) a process model can be described by using the process model language (PML), which is composed of two parts: a graphical notation and a textual notation.

the collaborative patterns are a useful tool for the process model developer, that the process modeler should be supported in the use of these patterns, that a graphical notation is a good way of supporting the process modeler, that the process modelling tool should support the use of the patterns, and that the process model should be supported during execution.
(a) collaborative work situations can be modelled by means of generic collaborative patterns, and (b) process-centred systems can be used as a platform for collaborative work.

the development of a generic process model for collaborative work.
modelling collaborative work, with the aim to improve the support of collaborative work.
the modelling of collaborative work and the design of process-centred systems for supporting this work.
